cards.explanation: The answer is the Israelites. Verse 1 says it plainly: the anger of the LORD burned against the Israelites. Achan, the man from Judah, is the one who took the devoted things. Yet the verse opens by saying the Israelites acted unfaithfully regarding them. I think that's the line that makes you stop and read it twice.

The answer is False. The spies say there's no need to send all the people, and that two or three thousand men are enough. They say the people of Ai are so few that Joshua need not wear out everyone. That's the exact confidence I have right before I say I'll only glance away from the oven for a second.

The answer is that they flee before the men of Ai. Verse 4 says about three thousand men went up, but they fled before the men of Ai. The spies had just called Ai's people so few, so I think running was the last thing anyone had in mind. The text says they fled, and in verse 5 the men of Ai chase them from the gate.

The answer is True. After the loss at Ai, the text says the hearts of the people melted and became like water. That's a picture of courage running right out of them, friends. About thirty-six men were lost, and the whole people felt it.

The answer is that Joshua wishes they had stayed on the other side of the Jordan. Joshua says, “If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan!” (Joshua 7:7). He says it out loud to the Lord GOD, with his face on the ground. I think his heart is heavy, and notice where he looks: back across the river.

The answer is that they will surround Israel and wipe out its name. Joshua says the Canaanites and all who live in the land will hear about this. Then, in his words, “…they will surround us and wipe out our name from the earth.” He's looking ahead and he doesn't like what he sees, friends. A lost battle feels like the start of something bigger.
The answer is True. Joshua ends with a question to God: “Then what will You do for Your great name?” He brings the whole mess straight to the LORD. He doesn't hide it or dress it up.

The answer is that they have been set apart for destruction. The LORD says the Israelites will turn their backs and run because they themselves have been set apart for destruction. That's the reason He gives for why they can't stand against their enemies. Notice He points at what's among them, not at Ai.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “I will no longer be with you unless you remove from among you whatever is devoted to destruction.” That's about as clear as it gets, friends. Everything depends on removing it.

The answer is that the LORD selects tribe by tribe down to one man. The LORD says the tribe He selects comes forward clan by clan, then family by family, then man by man. The circle keeps shrinking until it lands on one man. Nobody has to guess who it is.

The answer is that he transgressed the covenant of the LORD. The LORD says it's because he has transgressed the covenant of the LORD and committed an outrage in Israel. That's the reason given, and it's about the covenant. The text is heavy here, friends, and the reason it gives is plain.

The answer is confession. Joshua says, “…give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and make a confession to Him.” Then he adds that Achan should not hide it from him. Hiding is over, and telling the truth is on the table.

The answer is a cloak and silver and a gold bar. Achan says he saw a beautiful cloak from Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels. Then he says, “…I coveted them and took them.” He rattles off the list, weights and all, and I bet that list had been running through his head for a while.

The answer is coveted. Achan says, “…I coveted them and took them.” He sees something beautiful and wants it, and then his hands follow. He names it himself, friends, and I think that took a lot of nerve.
The answer is False. Achan says the things are hidden in the ground inside his tent, with the silver underneath. Nothing was buried outside the camp. The messengers run to the tent and find it all.

The answer is that they spread them out before the LORD. The text says they “…spread them out before the LORD.” (Joshua 7:23). Achan hid that stuff in a hole in the ground inside his tent. Now the cloak, the silver and the gold bar are laid out in the open like a yard sale nobody wanted. Verse 22 says it was all there with the silver underneath, just as he said. I know a little about being stuffed out of sight, friends, and I bet it never feels as safe as it looks.

The answer is False. Verse 26 says the LORD turned from His burning anger. The place is called the Valley of Achor to this day. This one is heavy, friends, and the text still tells us where the anger ends.
